audit_title: SURYOKTI Technical Audit: Maui Ocean Center (System 2105)

findings.offset_justification: Irradiance diurnal midpoint is 01:30 in logger timestamp across all seasons. Local solar noon at Maui (lon -156.512) is 12:26 HST. Shifting irradiance by -13 hours aligns sunrise (06:00/07:00), solar noon (12:00), and sunset (18:00/19:00) with local inverter generation. Physical correlation increases from -0.5018 (antiphase) to +0.8330.

findings.inverter_metric_unit_label: kWh (raw label, but represents average kW per interval)
findings.inverter_capacity_discrepancy: Inverters 01, 02, 07, 08 have individual peaks of 7-9 kW. Inverters 03, 05 peak around 14.6 kW. Inverters 04, 09, 10, 11 peak around 43.8 kW. Summing all 11 files yields a peak of 234 kW, which exceeds the stated 110 kW DC rating by 112%.
potential_causes: Double-counting: inverters 04, 09, 10, 11 may be sub-combiners aggregating strings 01-08.
Plant capacity upgrade after original 2016 registration not reflected in static metadata.
Inverter metrics 04, 09, 10, 11 representing multi-string combiner power rather than individual strings.
findings.recommendation: Use capacity-normalized metrics against actual observed peak (234 kW) or isolate non-overlapping string inverters to prevent overestimation.

observations.negative_lr_r2_cause: Linear Regression cannot capture the non-linear inverter clipping ceiling and seasonal panel degradation, resulting in massive overprediction in 2022-2023.
observations.model_selection: XGBoost achieves highest R2 (0.8658) and lowest RMSE (24.92 kW). Stacking achieves lowest MAE (12.29 kW). Stacking complexity is not justified by the 0.55 kW MAE difference; standalone XGBoost is recommended.

calibration_details.contamination_basis: Empirical physical rule violation rate on development split (2.83% sensor stuck readings during daylight)
calibration_details.ground_truth_disclaimer: NREL PVDAQ System 2105 lacks maintenance work order logs. Alarms represent physical/statistical anomalies, not verified hardware failures.
